# MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 Calibration checks - Machining induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-IH03

Scope
- This document defines the calibration check procedure for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03). It is intended for qualified maintenance and process personnel performing periodic verification and return-to-service checks after corrective work.
- The coil inspection interval for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 390 hours.
- The lubricant part number for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is CFW-LUB-725.
- This document supports compliance with preventive maintenance planning and process control; see related documents MM-P2-L3-IH03, QS-PROC-10, and SOP-P2-L3-01 for broader maintenance history, quality system requirements, and operational startup/shutdown steps respectively.

Tools
- Digital multimeter with AC/DC capability suitable for induction system verification.
- Clamp meter rated for induction heater current measurement.
- Insulation resistance tester (megger) appropriate for high-power winding checks.
- Hand tools for access panels and clamps; non-sparking set where required by line safety policy in SOP-P2-L3-01.
- Cleaning supplies and lint-free rags compatible with electrical components.
- Manufacturer-approved lubricant CFW-LUB-725 for bearing and mechanical lubrication tasks.
- Lockout/tagout hardware per plant policy referenced in QS-PROC-10.
- Calibration status tags and the inspection form template from MM-P2-L3-IH03.

Procedure
- Preparation and safety
  - Confirm authorization to work on EQ-P2-L3-IH03 per SOP-P2-L3-01. Coordinate with line control to hold process billets and establish a safe work window.
  - Apply lockout/tagout following QS-PROC-10 before opening access covers or disconnecting power. Verify absence of hazardous stored energy in capacitance banks and cooling lines.
  - Review the last coil inspection entry in MM-P2-L3-IH03 to note any recurring observations prior to starting checks.

- Visual inspection and mechanical checks
  - Inspect coil windings and busbar connections for signs of overheating, discoloration, deformation, or loose fasteners. Rationale: early visual detection reduces risk of progressive insulation degradation.
  - Inspect water-cooling connections and hose routing for leaks, kinks, or evidence of erosion near fittings. Rationale: proper cooling maintains thermal stability critical to repeatable heating results.
  - Check alignment and condition of billet guides and proximity sensors to ensure consistent billet positioning; correct minor misalignment per SOP-P2-L3-01 before electrical checks.
  - Apply manufacturer-approved lubricant CFW-LUB-725 only to designated bearing points; avoid contact with electrical insulation. Rationale: correct lubrication preserves mechanical movement without compromising electrical integrity.

- Electrical and calibration checks
  - Verify power input connections are torqued to the values specified in the OEM documentation located in MM-P2-L3-IH03 prior to energizing. Rationale: secure connections reduce resistive heating and measurement variability.
  - Measure winding insulation resistance with the insulation resistance tester. Compare to the baseline values recorded in MM-P2-L3-IH03; investigate if values deviate from historical trends. Rationale: insulation resistance trends predict impending winding failure.
  - With power applied under a controlled no-load condition as allowed by SOP-P2-L3-01, measure primary and secondary currents using the clamp meter and verify that readings match expected ratios in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Rationale: current balance and magnitude are primary calibration indicators for induction heating performance.
  - Check control system sensor calibrations per the interface specifications in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Calibrate temperature and flow sensors against calibrated reference equipment if drift is observed. Rationale: sensor accuracy directly affects process reproducibility.

- Functional verification
  - Perform a controlled heat cycle with a billet or calibrated test tag as described in SOP-P2-L3-01 and record outcome variables: heating time, sensor responses, and control setpoint adherence. Use the comparison method in MM-P2-L3-IH03 to assess performance against baseline behavior.
  - If anomalies are found, follow corrective work flow in QS-PROC-10 and update MM-P2-L3-IH03 records with actions taken, parts used, and observations.

Acceptance criteria
- No visible damage to coil windings or busbars; connectors secure and free of discoloration indicative of overheating. Refer to photographic examples in MM-P2-L3-IH03 for acceptable appearance.
- Cooling system intact with no active leaks; flow sensors and temperature sensors reporting within expected operational range as defined in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Insulation resistance values within acceptable trend band compared to prior entries in MM-P2-L3-IH03. If values fall outside the trend band, component replacement or repair is required before return to service.
- Electrical current and control responses consistent with baseline verification tests recorded in MM-P2-L3-IH03. Deviations must be investigated and documented under QS-PROC-10.
- Functional heat cycle produces repeatable billet temperature profile and control stability consistent with SOP-P2-L3-01 run parameters. Any failure to meet stability or repeatability requires root cause analysis and corrective action.

Background and rationale
- Induction heating relies on tight control of coil condition, electrical connections, and cooling to maintain repeatable thermal delivery. Regular inspection reduces unplanned downtime and part quality variation. The coil inspection interval of 390 hours balances wear progression and operational availability based on historical failure modes documented in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Lubrication with the specified lubricant CFW-LUB-725 protects mechanical components without degrading electrical insulation or contaminating billet paths.

Records to keep
- Complete the inspection checklist and attach measurement outputs to the equipment maintenance record in MM-P2-L3-IH03.
- Record any deviations, corrective actions, parts used, and approval signatures per QS-PROC-10.
- Retain functional verification logs and sensor calibration certificates as supporting evidence for process audits. Cross-reference entries to SOP-P2-L3-01 run sheets when calibrations are performed during operational windows.

Related documents
- MM-P2-L3-IH03
- QS-PROC-10
- SOP-P2-L3-01
